claim: Recreational drug use leads to compulsive substance abuse in some individuals.
source: Recreational drug use leads to compulsive substance abuse in some individuals.
evidence: This is a general statement about drug addiction presented in the abstract without specific experimental data or citations in this sentence.

claim: Persistent long-term potentiation (LTP) of excitatory synaptic transmission onto ventral tegmental area (VTA) dopamine (DA) neurons is a critical component of sustained drug seeking.
source: Studies on animal models of drug addiction indicate that persistent long-term potentiation (LTP) of excitatory synaptic transmission onto ventral tegmental area (VTA) dopamine (DA) neurons is a critical component of sustained drug seeking.
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to studies on animal models, indicating citation-based evidence.

claim: Translational control by eIF2α phosphorylation (p-eIF2α) regulates cocaine-induced LTP in the VTA.
source: Previously, we identified that translational control by eIF2α phosphorylation (p-eIF2α) regulates cocaine-induced LTP in the VTA (Huang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work (Huang et al., 2016).

claim: In mice with reduced p-eIF2α-mediated translation, cocaine induces persistent LTP in VTA DA neurons.
source: Here we report that in mice with reduced p-eIF2α-mediated translation, cocaine induces persistent LTP in VTA DA neurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Selectively inhibiting eIF2α-mediated translational control with a small molecule ISRIB prolongs cocaine-induced LTP.
source: Moreover, selectively inhibiting eIF2α-mediated translational control with a small molecule ISRIB, or knocking down oligophrenin-1—an mRNA whose translation is controlled by p-eIF2α—in the VTA also prolongs cocaine-induced LTP.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Knocking down oligophrenin-1 in the VTA prolongs cocaine-induced LTP.
source: Moreover, selectively inhibiting eIF2α-mediated translational control with a small molecule ISRIB, or knocking down oligophrenin-1—an mRNA whose translation is controlled by p-eIF2α—in the VTA also prolongs cocaine-induced LTP.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Persistent LTP induced by reduced p-eIF2α is mediated by the insertion of GluR2-lacking AMPARs.
source: This persistent LTP is mediated by the insertion of GluR2-lacking AMPARs.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: eIF2α-mediated translational control regulates the progression from transient to persistent cocaine-induced LTP.
source: Collectively, our findings suggest that eIF2α-mediated translational control regulates the progression from transient to persistent cocaine-induced LTP.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Drug addiction is a complex behavioral disorder that starts with recreational use and, in some people, progresses to compulsive drug-seeking.
source: Drug addiction is a complex behavioral disorder that starts with recreational use and, in some people, progresses to compulsive drug-seeking (Hyman, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hyman, 2005.

claim: Repeated drug use leads to long-lasting changes in neuronal structure and function in key reward areas in addicts.
source: In addicts, repeated drug use leads to long-lasting changes in neuronal structure and function in key reward areas (Koob and Volkow, 2010), which have emerged as cellular correlates of drug addiction (Chen et al., 2008; Lüscher and Malenka, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Koob and Volkow, 2010; Chen et al., 2008; Lüscher and Malenka, 2011.

claim: Activity-dependent changes in synaptic strength in the VTA constitute the initial synaptic adaptations observed after drug exposure.
source: These activity-dependent changes in synaptic strength in the VTA constitute the initial synaptic adaptations observed after drug exposure (Lüscher and Malenka, 2011; Schilstrom et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lüscher and Malenka, 2011; Schilstrom et al., 2006.

claim: A single injection of cocaine given 24 hr before recording induces an LTP that is manifested as an increase in the ratio of AMPAR- to NMDAR-mediated EPSCs onto DA neurons in the VTA.
source: For instance, a single injection of cocaine (or other drugs of abuse) given 24 hr before recording induces an LTP that is manifested as an increase in the ratio of the amplitude of α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor (AMPAR)- to N-methyl D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR)-mediated excitatory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs) onto DA neurons in the VTA (Ungless et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ungless et al., 2001.

claim: LTP induced by an acute injection of cocaine typically lasts up to five days, but it returns to baseline after 10 days.
source: LTP induced by an acute injection of cocaine typically lasts up to five days, but it returns to baseline after 10 days (Borgland et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Borgland et al., 2004.

claim: Short-lasting LTP is associated with the insertion of AMPARs lacking the GluR2 subunit, as demonstrated by an increased inward rectification of postsynaptic AMPAR currents.
source: This short-lasting LTP is associated with the insertion of AMPARs lacking the GluR2 subunit, as demonstrated by an increased inward rectification of postsynaptic AMPAR currents (Bellone and Lüscher, 2006; Engblom et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bellone and Lüscher, 2006; Engblom et al., 2008.

claim: LTP persists for several weeks following cocaine self-administration, in contrast to passive cocaine administration.
source: Interestingly, in contrast to passive cocaine administration, LTP persists for several weeks following self-administration (Chen et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2008.

claim: Drug-induced persistent changes in synaptic strength in the VTA may represent the cellular process driving the progression from recreational to compulsive drug use.
source: Thus, these drug-induced persistent changes in synaptic strength in the VTA may represent the cellular process driving the progression from recreational to compulsive drug use.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the cited findings.

claim: Pharmacological activation of metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluRs) with DHPG inhibits cocaine-induced LTP in VTA DA neurons.
source: Furthermore, pharmacological activation of metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluRs) with dihydroxyphenylglycine (DHPG), a group I mGluR agonist, inhibits cocaine-induced LTP in VTA DA neurons (Bellone and Lüscher, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bellone and Lüscher, 2006.

claim: mGluR-mediated long-term depression (mGluR-LTD) reverses drug-evoked LTP and inward rectification in VTA DA neurons by internalization of AMPARs.
source: This inhibition is attributed to the opposing effect of mGluR-mediated long-term depression (mGluR-LTD), which reverses drug-evoked LTP and inward rectification in VTA DA neurons by internalization of AMPARs (Bellone and Lüscher, 2006; Lüscher and Huber, 2010; Lüscher and Malenka, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bellone and Lüscher, 2006; Lüscher and Huber, 2010; Lüscher and Malenka, 2011.

claim: Cocaine induces LTP and reduces p-eIF2α levels in the VTA.
source: First, cocaine induces LTP and reduces p-eIF2α levels in the VTA (Huang et al., 2016), whereas DHPG elicits mGluR1/5-induced LTD and increases p-eIF2α (Di Prisco et al., 2014; Trinh et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Huang et al., 2016.

claim: DHPG elicits mGluR1/5-induced LTD and increases p-eIF2α.
source: First, cocaine induces LTP and reduces p-eIF2α levels in the VTA (Huang et al., 2016), whereas DHPG elicits mGluR1/5-induced LTD and increases p-eIF2α (Di Prisco et al., 2014; Trinh et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Di Prisco et al., 2014; Trinh et al., 2014.

claim: Genetic and pharmacological inhibition of p-eIF2α-mediated translational control facilitates the induction of LTP by blocking mGluR-LTD in VTA DA neurons.
source: Second, both genetic and pharmacological inhibition of p-eIF2α-mediated translational control facilitates the induction of LTP by blocking mGluR-LTD in VTA DA neurons (Huang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Huang et al., 2016.

claim: Pharmacologically increasing p-eIF2α levels induces mGluR-LTD and prevents cocaine-induced LTP in VTA DA neurons.
source: Finally, pharmacologically increasing p-eIF2α levels induces mGluR-LTD and prevents cocaine-induced LTP in VTA DA neurons (Huang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Huang et al., 2016.

claim: mGluR-LTD blocks the persistence of cocaine-induced LTP.
source: Given that mGluR-LTD blocks the persistence of cocaine-induced LTP (Mameli et al., 2009), and our previous finding that p-eIF2α–mediated translational control regulates both forms of long-lasting plasticity (Huang et al., 2016), we examined whether the same translational control program regulates the shift from a relatively transient cocaine-induced LTP to a more persistent one in VTA DA neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mameli et al., 2009.

claim: Single exposure to cocaine in rodents induces LTP that lasts for five days, but decays to baseline after 10 days.
source: Single or repeated exposure to cocaine in rodents induces LTP that lasts for five days, but decays to baseline after 10 days (Borgland et al., 2004; Kauer and Malenka, 2007; Mameli et al., 2009; Ungless et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Borgland et al., 2004; Kauer and Malenka, 2007; Mameli et al., 2009; Ungless et al., 2001.

claim: Repeated exposure to cocaine in rodents induces LTP that lasts for five days, but decays to baseline after 10 days.
source: Single or repeated exposure to cocaine in rodents induces LTP that lasts for five days, but decays to baseline after 10 days (Borgland et al., 2004; Kauer and Malenka, 2007; Mameli et al., 2009; Ungless et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Borgland et al., 2004; Kauer and Malenka, 2007; Mameli et al., 2009; Ungless et al., 2001.

claim: Both single and multiple injections of cocaine (10 mg/kg) reduced p-eIF2α levels in the VTA.
source: Interestingly, both acute and repeated exposure to cocaine reduced p-eIF2α levels in the VTA (Figure 1b and c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b and c.

claim: Single injection of cocaine (10 mg/kg) reduced p-eIF2α levels in the VTA (p<0.001, n = 6 per group, t10 = 4.640).
source: (b-c) Both single (10 mg/kg; p<0.001, n = 6 per group, t10 = 4.640) or multiple (five) injections of cocaine (10 mg/kg, p<0.05, n = 3 per group, t4 = 4.329) reduced p-eIF2α levels in the VTA of adult mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: Multiple (five) injections of cocaine (10 mg/kg) reduced p-eIF2α levels in the VTA (p<0.05, n = 3 per group, t4 = 4.329).
source: (b-c) Both single (10 mg/kg; p<0.001, n = 6 per group, t10 = 4.640) or multiple (five) injections of cocaine (10 mg/kg, p<0.05, n = 3 per group, t4 = 4.329) reduced p-eIF2α levels in the VTA of adult mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: Eif2s1S/A heterozygous mutant mice have reduced p-eIF2α levels in the VTA.
source: To test whether the same process is involved in the persistence of LTP, we first employed Eif2s1S/A heterozygous mutant mice, in which a single phosphorylation site in eIF2α (encoded by the Eif2s1 gene) at Serine-51 is replaced by alanine. These mice have reduced p-eIF2α levels in the VTA (Huang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Huang et al., 2016.

claim: In control WT mice, cocaine (10 mg/kg) elicited an LTP that lasted five days but not 14 days after withdrawal.
source: As previously reported (Borgland et al., 2004), in control slices, cocaine (10 mg/kg) elicited an LTP that lasted five days (5d) but not 14d after withdrawal (Figure 2a and c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a and c, and is consistent with previous reports (Borgland et al., 2004).

claim: In VTA slices from Eif2s1S/A mice, LTP was greater at five days compared to WT controls and was still present 14 days after the last cocaine injection.
source: By contrast, in VTA slices from Eif2s1S/A mice, LTP was greater at five days compared to WT controls and was still present and not significantly changed 14 days after the last cocaine injection (Figure 2b and c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2b and c.

claim: Cocaine-induced LTP in the VTA persisted for at least 40 days in Eif2s1S/A mice.
source: Indeed, cocaine-induced LTP in the VTA persisted for at least 40 days in Eif2s1S/A mice, which was as long as we continued the withdrawal period (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: A decrease in eIF2α phosphorylation facilitates the progression from transient to persistent cocaine-induced LTP.
source: Thus, a decrease in eIF2α phosphorylation facilitates the progression from transient to persistent cocaine-induced LTP.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figure 2.

claim: Increased AMPAR/NMDAR ratios lasted only five days in cocaine-injected WT mice (10 mg/kg; 5d, p<0.01, n = 11/9/10 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,27 = 7.82).
source: (a–c) Increased AMPAR/NMDAR ratios lasted only five days in cocaine-injected WT mice (10 mg/kg; 5d, p<0.01, n = 11/9/10 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,27 = 7.82), but persisted >14 days in cocaine-injected Eif2s1S/A mice (5d, p<0.001; 14d, p<0.001, n = 9/8/10 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,24 = 13.31).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: Increased AMPAR/NMDAR ratios persisted >14 days in cocaine-injected Eif2s1S/A mice (5d, p<0.001; 14d, p<0.001, n = 9/8/10 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,24 = 13.31).
source: (a–c) Increased AMPAR/NMDAR ratios lasted only five days in cocaine-injected WT mice (10 mg/kg; 5d, p<0.01, n = 11/9/10 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,27 = 7.82), but persisted >14 days in cocaine-injected Eif2s1S/A mice (5d, p<0.001; 14d, p<0.001, n = 9/8/10 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,24 = 13.31).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: Cocaine (10 mg/kg, i.p.) increased AMPAR/NMDAR ratio in GFP-positive cells (in which eIF2α cannot be phosphorylated), both at five and at 14 days post-injection (5d, p<0.001; 14d, p<0.001, n = 5/6/6 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,14 = 8.30).
source: (d–f) Similarly, cocaine (10 mg/kg, i.p.) increased AMPAR/NMDAR ratio in GFP-positive cells (in which eIF2α cannot be phosphorylated), both at five and at 14 days post-injection (5d, p<0.001; 14d, p<0.001 , n = 5/6/6 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,14 = 8.30), compared to control GFP-negative cells (5d, p<0.05, n = 5/8/5 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,15 = 4.78) from Eif2s1A/A;ftg mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 2d-f.

claim: In control GFP-negative cells from Eif2s1A/A;ftg mice, cocaine increased AMPAR/NMDAR ratio at five days (5d, p<0.05, n = 5/8/5 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,15 = 4.78) but not at 14 days.
source: (d–f) Similarly, cocaine (10 mg/kg, i.p.) increased AMPAR/NMDAR ratio in GFP-positive cells (in which eIF2α cannot be phosphorylated), both at five and at 14 days post-injection (5d, p<0.001; 14d, p<0.001 , n = 5/6/6 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,14 = 8.30), compared to control GFP-negative cells (5d, p<0.05, n = 5/8/5 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,15 = 4.78) from Eif2s1A/A;ftg mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 2d-f.

claim: Forty days after i.p. cocaine injections (10 mg/kg), a significant LTP was observed in VTA DA neurons from Eif2s1S/A mice, but not in control littermates (p<0.05, n = 11/5 WT 40d cocaine/Eif2s1S/A 40d cocaine, t14 = 2.25).
source: Forty days after i.p. cocaine injections (10 mg/kg), a significant LTP was observed in VTA DA neurons from Eif2s1S/A mice, but not in control littermates (p<0.05, n = 11/5 WT 40d cocaine/Eif2s1S/A 40d cocaine, t14 = 2.25, ).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: In GFP- (control) VTA DA neurons, cocaine-evoked LTP lasted five days, but returned to baseline by 14 days after withdrawal.
source: As expected, in GFP- (control) VTA DA neurons, cocaine-evoked LTP lasted five days, but returned to baseline by 14 days after withdrawal (Figure 2d and f).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2d and f.

claim: In GFP+ VTA DA neurons lacking p-eIF2α, LTP was much greater at five days and persisted for at least 14 days.
source: However, in GFP+ VTA DA neurons lacking p-eIF2α, LTP was much greater at five days and persisted for at least 14 days (Figure 2e and f), highlighting the cell-autonomous effect of eIF2α phosphorylation on the persistence of LTP.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2e and f.

claim: The effect of eIF2α phosphorylation on the persistence of LTP is cell-autonomous.
source: However, in GFP+ VTA DA neurons lacking p-eIF2α, LTP was much greater at five days and persisted for at least 14 days (Figure 2e and f), highlighting the cell-autonomous effect of eIF2α phosphorylation on the persistence of LTP.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data comparing GFP+ and GFP- neurons.

claim: Cocaine-induced synaptic potentiation in VTA DA neurons is accompanied by a shift in the subunit composition of postsynaptic AMPARs.
source: Cocaine-induced synaptic potentiation in VTA DA neurons is accompanied by a shift in the subunit composition of postsynaptic AMPARs (Bellone and Lüscher, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bellone and Lüscher, 2006.

claim: Under normal conditions, postsynaptic AMPA-type currents are mediated by low conductance calcium-impermeable GluR1/GluR2 heteromeric receptors that are characterized by linear AMPAR current-voltage relationships.
source: Under normal conditions, postsynaptic AMPA-type currents are mediated by low conductance calcium-impermeable GluR1/GluR2 heteromeric receptors that are characterized by linear AMPAR current-voltage relationships.
evidence: This is established knowledge about AMPAR properties.

claim: Exposure to cocaine results in the postsynaptic insertion of high conductance calcium-permeable AMPA receptors that lack GluR2 subunits and are consequently inwardly rectifying.
source: Exposure to cocaine results in the postsynaptic insertion of high conductance calcium-permeable AMPA receptors that lack GluR2 subunits and are consequently inwardly rectifying (manifested as smaller AMPAR EPSCs measured at positive holding potentials versus those measured at corresponding negative potentials).
evidence: This is established knowledge about cocaine's effects on AMPARs.

claim: GluR2-lacking AMPARs are sensitive to blockade by intracellular polyamines.
source: In addition, GluR2-lacking AMPARs are sensitive to blockade by intracellular polyamines (Iino et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Iino et al., 1996.

claim: Cocaine increased inward rectification in control VTA DA neurons (Eif2s1S/S) at five days post-injection.
source: By recording EPSCs in VTA DA neurons at −70, 0, and +40 mV to calculate the rectification index, we found that cocaine increased inward rectification in control VTA DA neurons (Eif2s1S/S; Figures 3a,c and e) and to a greater degree in slices from Eif2s1S/A mice (Figures 3b,d and e) at five days post-injection.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3a, c, and e.

claim: Cocaine increased inward rectification to a greater degree in slices from Eif2s1S/A mice at five days post-injection.
source: By recording EPSCs in VTA DA neurons at −70, 0, and +40 mV to calculate the rectification index, we found that cocaine increased inward rectification in control VTA DA neurons (Eif2s1S/S; Figures 3a,c and e) and to a greater degree in slices from Eif2s1S/A mice (Figures 3b,d and e) at five days post-injection.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3b, d, and e.

claim: 14 days after cocaine treatment, EPSCs were non-rectifying in WT controls.
source: However, 14 days after cocaine treatment, EPSCs were non-rectifying in WT controls (Figures 3a,c and e), whereas Eif2s1S/A mice retained their inwardly-rectifying properties (Figures 3b,d and e).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3a, c, and e.

claim: 14 days after cocaine treatment, Eif2s1S/A mice retained their inwardly-rectifying properties.
source: However, 14 days after cocaine treatment, EPSCs were non-rectifying in WT controls (Figures 3a,c and e), whereas Eif2s1S/A mice retained their inwardly-rectifying properties (Figures 3b,d and e).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3b, d, and e.

claim: Potentiated EPSCs in cocaine-treated Eif2s1S/A mice measured at 14 days were sensitive to Joro spider toxin (JST, 500 nM).
source: Moreover, potentiated EPSCs in cocaine-treated Eif2s1S/A mice measured at 14 days were sensitive to two blockers of GluR2-lacking AMPARs, Joro spider toxin (JST (Iino et al., 1996), 500 nM; Figure 3—figure supplement 1a) and 1-Naphthyl acetyl spermine (NASPM (Tsubokawa et al., 1995), 50 μM; Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Potentiated EPSCs in cocaine-treated Eif2s1S/A mice measured at 14 days were sensitive to 1-Naphthyl acetyl spermine (NASPM, 50 μM).
source: Moreover, potentiated EPSCs in cocaine-treated Eif2s1S/A mice measured at 14 days were sensitive to two blockers of GluR2-lacking AMPARs, Joro spider toxin (JST (Iino et al., 1996), 500 nM; Figure 3—figure supplement 1a) and 1-Naphthyl acetyl spermine (NASPM (Tsubokawa et al., 1995), 50 μM; Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Postsynaptic insertion of GluR2-lacking AMPARs underlies the persistent LTP in VTA DA neurons with reduced p-eIF2α levels.
source: We conclude that postsynaptic insertion of GluR2-lacking AMPARs underlies the persistent LTP in VTA DA neurons with reduced p-eIF2α levels.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on rectification and blocker sensitivity.

claim: Cocaine-induced rectification lasts only five days in control mice (5d, p<0.001, n = 12/10/7 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,26 = 32.02).
source: I-V plots (c–d) and summaries (e) illustrate that cocaine-induced rectification lasts only five days in control mice (5d, p<0.001, n = 12/10/7 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,26 = 32.02) but persists at least 14 days in Eif2s1S/A mice (5d, p<0.05; 14d, p<0.05, n = 8/8/10 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,23 = 17.21).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: Cocaine-induced rectification persists at least 14 days in Eif2s1S/A mice (5d, p<0.05; 14d, p<0.05, n = 8/8/10 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,23 = 17.21).
source: I-V plots (c–d) and summaries (e) illustrate that cocaine-induced rectification lasts only five days in control mice (5d, p<0.001, n = 12/10/7 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,26 = 32.02) but persists at least 14 days in Eif2s1S/A mice (5d, p<0.05; 14d, p<0.05, n = 8/8/10 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,23 = 17.21).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: At 14 days after cocaine injection, Joro Spider Toxin (JST, 500 nM) depressed EPSCs in VTA neurons from Eif2s1S/A mice (p<0.001, n = 5, t8 = 23.67), but not in neurons from control littermates (p = 0.42, n = 5, t8 = 0.857).
source: (a) At 14 days after cocaine injection, Joro Spider Toxin (JST, 500 nM), a polyamine that blocks GluR2-lacking AMPA current, depressed EPSCs (recorded at −70 mV) in VTA neurons from Eif2s1S/A mice (p<0.001, n = 5, t8 = 23.67), but not in neurons from control littermates (p = 0.42, n = 5, t8 = 0.857).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a.

claim: At 14 days after cocaine injection, 1-Naphthyl acetyl spermine (NASPM, 50 μM) depressed EPSCs in VTA neurons from Eif2s1S/A mice (p<0.01, n = 5, t8 = 5.992), but not in neurons from control littermates (p = 0.22, n = 5, t8 = 1.441).
source: (b) At 14 days after cocaine injection, 1-Naphthyl acetyl spermine (NASPM, 50 μM), a synthetic analog of JST that also blocks GluR2-lacking AMPA current, depressed EPSCs (recorded at −70 mV) in VTA neurons from Eif2s1S/A mice (p<0.01, n = 5, t8 = 5.992), but not in neurons from control littermates (p = 0.22, n = 5, t8 = 1.441).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Phosphorylation of eIF2α inhibits general protein synthesis by inhibiting the guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) eIF2B.
source: While phosphorylation of eIF2α inhibits general protein synthesis by inhibiting the guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) eIF2B, it also increases the translation of specific mRNAs (Buffington et al., 2014; Ron and Harding, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Buffington et al., 2014; Ron and Harding, 2007.

claim: Phosphorylation of eIF2α increases the translation of specific mRNAs.
source: While phosphorylation of eIF2α inhibits general protein synthesis by inhibiting the guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) eIF2B, it also increases the translation of specific mRNAs (Buffington et al., 2014; Ron and Harding, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Buffington et al., 2014; Ron and Harding, 2007.

claim: ISRIB promotes eIF2B activity resulting in selective reversal of p-eIF2α-mediated translational events.
source: In our previous study, we used the small molecule inhibitor ISRIB, which promotes eIF2B activity resulting in selective reversal of p-eIF2α-mediated translational events (Sekine et al., 2015; Sidrauski et al., 2013, 2015) and, consequently, makes adult mice more susceptible to the synaptic and behavioral effects of a sub-threshold dose of cocaine (Huang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Sekine et al., 2015; Sidrauski et al., 2013, 2015.

claim: ISRIB makes adult mice more susceptible to the synaptic and behavioral effects of a sub-threshold dose of cocaine.
source: In our previous study, we used the small molecule inhibitor ISRIB, which promotes eIF2B activity resulting in selective reversal of p-eIF2α-mediated translational events (Sekine et al., 2015; Sidrauski et al., 2013, 2015) and, consequently, makes adult mice more susceptible to the synaptic and behavioral effects of a sub-threshold dose of cocaine (Huang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Huang et al., 2016.

claim: Cocaine induced both persistent LTP and inward rectification only in VTA DA neurons from ISRIB-injected mice.
source: Consistent with our findings with Eif2s1S/A mice, cocaine induced both persistent LTP (Figure 4a–c) and inward rectification (Figure 4d–h) only in VTA DA neurons from ISRIB-injected mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Cocaine-induced increase in AMPAR/NMDAR ratios lasted only five days in control mice (5d, p<0.05, n = 5/5/5 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,12 = 8.38), but persisted at least 14 days in ISRIB-injected mice (5d, p<0.05; 14d, p<0.05, n = 5/5/5 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,12 = 6.40).
source: (a–c) Cocaine-induced increase in AMPAR/NMDAR ratios lasted only five days in control mice (5d, p<0.05, n = 5/5/5 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,12 = 8.38), but persisted at least 14 days in ISRIB-injected mice (5d, p<0.05; 14d, p<0.05, n = 5/5/5 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,12 = 6.40).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 4a-c.

claim: Cocaine-induced rectification lasts only five days in vehicle-injected mice (5d, p<0.05, n = 4/4/4 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,9 = 7.12), but persists at least 14 days in ISRIB-injected mice (5d, p<0.05; 14d, p<0.05, n = 4/4/4 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,9 = 7.53).
source: I-V plots (f–g) and summaries (h) illustrate that cocaine-induced rectification lasts only five days in vehicle-injected mice (5d, p<0.05, n = 4/4/4 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,9 = 7.12), but persists at least 14 days in ISRIB-injected mice (5d, p<0.05; 14d, p<0.05, n = 4/4/4 saline/5d cocaine/14d cocaine, F2,9 = 7.53).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 4f-h.

claim: p-eIF2α-mediated synthesis of oligophrenin-1 (OPHN1) blocks cocaine-induced LTP.
source: Given that p-eIF2α-mediated synthesis of oligophrenin-1 (OPHN1) blocks cocaine-induced LTP (Huang et al., 2016), we next asked whether a reduction in OPHN1 levels in the VTA would also prolong cocaine-induced LTP.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Huang et al., 2016.

claim: Knocking down OPHN1 in the VTA prolonged cocaine-induced LTP to 14 days after cocaine withdrawal (p<0.001, n = 9/8 control-shRNA/Ophn1-shRNA, t15 = 4.986).
source: (i) Knocking down OPHN1 in the VTA prolonged cocaine-induced LTP to 14 days after cocaine withdrawal (p<0.001, n = 9/8 control-shRNA/Ophn1-shRNA, t15 = 4.986).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 4i.

claim: In OPHN1-deficient VTA DA neurons, cocaine-induced LTP persisted for at least 14 days.
source: As expected, in OPHN1-deficient, but not in control VTA DA neurons, cocaine-induced LTP persisted for at least 14 days (Figure 4i).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4i.

claim: Cocaine-evoked LTP becomes persistent when p-eIF2α-mediated translation of OPHN1 is repressed.
source: These data support the notion that cocaine-evoked LTP becomes persistent when p-eIF2α-mediated translation of OPHN1 is repressed.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on OPHN1 knockdown.

claim: Drug addiction is a disorder involving maladaptive plasticity in key reward areas of the brain.
source: Drug addiction is a disorder involving maladaptive plasticity in key reward areas of the brain (Bowers et al., 2010; Hyman et al., 2006; Kauer and Malenka, 2007; Lüscher and Malenka, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bowers et al., 2010; Hyman et al., 2006; Kauer and Malenka, 2007; Lüscher and Malenka, 2011.

claim: mGluR-LTD in VTA DA neurons blocks cocaine-evoked LTP in these same cells by replacing GluR2-lacking calcium permeable AMPARs with GluR2-containing receptors.
source: Two studies revealed that mGluR-LTD in VTA DA neurons blocks cocaine-evoked LTP in these same cells by replacing GluR2-lacking calcium permeable AMPARs with GluR2-containing receptors (Bellone and Lüscher, 2006; Mameli et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bellone and Lüscher, 2006; Mameli et al., 2007.

claim: mGluR-LTD depends on new protein synthesis, unlike NMDA-induced LTD.
source: Unlike NMDA-induced LTD, mGluR-LTD depends on new protein synthesis (Lüscher and Huber, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lüscher and Huber, 2010.

claim: eIF2α-mediated translational control is necessary and sufficient for mGluR-LTD in both the hippocampus and the VTA.
source: We have previously shown that eIF2α-mediated translational control is necessary and sufficient for mGluR-LTD in both the hippocampus and the VTA (Di Prisco et al., 2014; Huang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Di Prisco et al., 2014; Huang et al., 2016.

claim: Treatment with the mTORC1 inhibitor rapamycin blocks mGluR-LTD in the VTA.
source: Treatment with the mTORC1 inhibitor rapamycin blocks mGluR-LTD in the VTA (Mameli et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mameli et al., 2007.

claim: During mGluR-LTD, activation of mGluRs by DHPG triggers the synthesis of OPHN1 in a p-eIF2α-dependent manner.
source: During mGluR-LTD, activation of mGluRs by DHPG triggers the synthesis of OPHN1 (Nadif Kasri et al., 2011) in a p-eIF2α-dependent manner (Di Prisco et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nadif Kasri et al., 2011; Di Prisco et al., 2014.

claim: OPHN1 translation is required to induce mGluR-LTD.
source: If rapamycin exerted its effects on mGluR-LTD by blocking OPHN1 translation, which is required to induce mGluR-LTD (Di Prisco et al., 2014; Nadif Kasri et al., 2011), these seemingly contradictory findings would be easily reconciled.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Di Prisco et al., 2014; Nadif Kasri et al., 2011.

claim: Inhibition of mGluR-LTD by genetic disruption of Homer1C-mGluR1 interaction prolongs cocaine-induced LTP from five days to seven days.
source: Inhibition of mGluR-LTD by genetic disruption of Homer1C-mGluR1 interaction or by treatment with an antagonist of group I mGluRs [1-aminoindan-1,5-dicarboxylic acid (AIDA)] has been shown to prolong cocaine-induced LTP from five days to seven days (Mameli et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mameli et al., 2009.

claim: Treatment with an antagonist of group I mGluRs (AIDA) prolongs cocaine-induced LTP from five days to seven days.
source: Inhibition of mGluR-LTD by genetic disruption of Homer1C-mGluR1 interaction or by treatment with an antagonist of group I mGluRs [1-aminoindan-1,5-dicarboxylic acid (AIDA)] has been shown to prolong cocaine-induced LTP from five days to seven days (Mameli et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mameli et al., 2009.

claim: By suppressing p-eIF2α-mediated mGluR-LTD, cocaine induces an LTP that lasted up to 40 days and was mediated by the insertion of GluR2-lacking receptors.
source: By suppressing p-eIF2α-mediated mGluR-LTD, we found that cocaine induces an LTP that lasted up to 40 days and was mediated by the insertion of GluR2-lacking receptors.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claim: Like self-administration of cocaine, passive injections of cocaine in mice with reduced p-eIF2α-mediated translational control elicit a synaptic potentiation that lasts for weeks.
source: Thus, like self-administration of cocaine (Chen et al., 2008), passive injections of cocaine in mice with reduced p-eIF2α-mediated translational control elicit a synaptic potentiation that lasts for weeks.
evidence: This is a comparison between the current findings and previous work (Chen et al., 2008).

claim: p-eIF2α-mediated translation prevents the progression from transient to persistent cocaine-induced LTP in VTA DA neurons.
source: Our findings indicate that p-eIF2α-mediated translation prevents the progression from transient to persistent cocaine-induced LTP in VTA DA neurons, thus regulating synaptic potentiation that is believed to underlie compulsive drug seeking (Chen et al., 2008; Lüscher and Malenka, 2011; Mameli et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Persistent LTP in VTA DA neurons is believed to underlie compulsive drug seeking.
source: Our findings indicate that p-eIF2α-mediated translation prevents the progression from transient to persistent cocaine-induced LTP in VTA DA neurons, thus regulating synaptic potentiation that is believed to underlie compulsive drug seeking (Chen et al., 2008; Lüscher and Malenka, 2011; Mameli et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2008; Lüscher and Malenka, 2011; Mameli et al., 2009.

claim: The vulnerability to compulsive drug abuse in humans has been linked to deficits in cortico-striatal processing.
source: In humans, the vulnerability to compulsive drug abuse has been linked to deficits in cortico-striatal processing (Ersche et al., 2011; Volkow et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ersche et al., 2011; Volkow et al., 2009.

claim: Mesolimbic neuronal reward responses are altered in human smokers carrying a single nucleotide polymorphism in the Eif2s1 gene.
source: We have recently found that mesolimbic neuronal reward responses are altered in human smokers carrying a single nucleotide polymorphism in the Eif2s1 gene (which encodes eIF2α) (Placzek et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Placzek et al., 2016.

claim: In cocaine addicts, persistent activity-dependent changes in synaptic strength in the VTA are likely to produce long-lasting changes in synaptic function in downstream structures, such as the nucleus accumbens (NAc) and prefrontal cortex (PFC).
source: Finally, in cocaine addicts, persistent activity-dependent changes in synaptic strength in the VTA are likely to produce long-lasting changes in synaptic function in downstream structures, such as the nucleus accumbens (NAc) and prefrontal cortex (PFC).
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on known neural circuitry.

claim: Enhancing mGluR signaling in the NAc blocks cocaine relapse and craving.
source: Given that enhancing mGluR signaling in the NAc blocks cocaine relapse and craving (Loweth et al., 2013) and that eIF2α is a key regulator of mGluR-LTD and cocaine-induced LTP, we propose that modulators of p-eIF2α-mediated translational control may be useful in the treatment of cocaine addiction.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Loweth et al., 2013.

claim: Modulators of p-eIF2α-mediated translational control may be useful in the treatment of cocaine addiction.
source: Given that enhancing mGluR signaling in the NAc blocks cocaine relapse and craving (Loweth et al., 2013) and that eIF2α is a key regulator of mGluR-LTD and cocaine-induced LTP, we propose that modulators of p-eIF2α-mediated translational control may be useful in the treatment of cocaine addiction.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the findings and cited literature.

claim: All experiments were conducted using C57Bl/6J male and female mice.
source: All experiments were conducted using C57Bl/6J male and female mice.
evidence: This is a methodological statement about the experimental subjects.

claim: Eif2s1S/A and Eif2s1A/A;ftg mice were previously described.
source: Eif2s1S/A and Eif2s1A/A;ftg mice were previously described (Di Prisco et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Di Prisco et al., 2014.

claim: Cell phenotype was determined by measuring the width (>1.0 ms) of the cell-attached action potential.
source: After establishing a gigaohm seal (>2 GΩ) and recording stable spontaneous firing in cell-attached, voltage clamp mode (−70 mV holding potential), cell phenotype was determined by measuring the width (>1.0 ms) of the cell-attached action potential (Chieng et al., 2011; Ford et al., 2006).
evidence: This methodological claim is supported by citations to Chieng et al., 2011; Ford et al., 2006.

claim: AMPAR/NMDAR ratios were calculated as previously described.
source: AMPAR/NMDAR ratios were calculated as previously described (Ungless et al., 2001).
evidence: This methodological claim is supported by a citation to Ungless et al., 2001.
